subject: Re: StrataCorp MSA & Order Form — IP ownership mapping and proposed positions
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@stratacorp.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: StrataCorp Legal <legal@stratacorp.com>
Date: Wed, 01 May 2029 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial redlines + questions on IP/training rights

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal ran our first pass on the MSA and order form and surfaced a couple of items we need clarified before we can route to procurement:

1) Section 4.2 (Output ownership) — we want a clearer assignment of output for any productized feature that embeds Redwood output into our UI.
2) Training/data use — your team previously said Redwood would not train on customer data by default; we need that reflected in the Order Form and an opt-in path if we later agree to any model tuning.
3) Feedback license — can Redwood take anonymized feedback to improve models, and if so, what downstream rights do you claim?

I've attached our redlines and a short mapping file with examples. Can your team propose language for each point by EOD Thursday? Procurement expects answers before starting the signature packet.

Appreciate it — Alyssa

Attachments: StrataCorp_MSA_redlines_v2.docx, IP_mapping_matrix.xlsx

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@stratacorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 May 2029 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial redlines + questions on IP/training rights

Alyssa — thanks for the clear summary and the example matrix. We'll put together proposed, minimally invasive language for each of the three asks.

Quick plan:
- We (legal + product) will propose a short customer-friendly clause for Output Ownership that preserves StrataCorp productization rights while keeping our operational telemetry and service improvements intact.
- We will add an explicit "no-training-by-default" statement in the Order Form and an opt-in appendix for any model tuning (with scope, approval, and data handling).
- For feedback, we'll propose an anonymized feedback license limited to internal model quality work and forbidding re-use for customer-specific model replication; we can show the exact redline.

I'll get a draft to you by Thursday EOD PT. Looping in Karthik and Laura for legal language and Ben for implementation constraints (telemetry/evidence).

Cheers,
Rachel Kim
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 May 2029 09:09:15 -0700
Subject: Internal — Sourcing suggested redlines for StrataCorp (DEAL-7842)

Team — Alyssa sent StrataCorp's redlines (attached). Procurement wants our positions asap. My proposed lean positions below; please pick fights only where necessary.

1) Output Ownership (Section 4.2):
- Proposal: "Customer owns final outputs they receive and embed in their product. Redwood retains the right to use aggregated service telemetry and anonymized metrics for service improvements; Redwood will not claim ownership of Customer-generated content."
- Risk: Procurement may press for assignment of derivative rights for productized features. Recommend we avoid assignment language.

2) Training / Data Use:
- Proposal: Add to Order Form: "Redwood will not use Customer data for model training, fine-tuning, or model weights updates unless Customer provides explicit, written opt-in via an appendix that specifies scope, retention, and security controls."
- Risk: This is already our platform default; making it explicit is low risk but require ops confirmation for opt-in process.

3) Feedback License:
- Proposal: "Customer grants Redwood a limited, perpetual, royalty-free license to use feedback (de-identified and aggregated) to improve or retrain Redwood models, provided such use does not enable re-creation of Customer proprietary datasets or outputs. Redwood will not sell or sublicense Customer-specific outputs to third parties."
- Risk: Legal will ask for boundaries; propose adding examples of forbidden uses.

Ben — can you confirm the telemetry we collect today and whether we can provide an 'opt-out-by-tag' on customer traffic if requested?
Karthik/Laura — please mark edits in the attached MSA redline, keeping the language tight.

Thanks — R

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 May 2029 11:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal — Sourcing suggested redlines for StrataCorp (DEAL-7842)

Agree with Rachel's framing. Draft redlines below to start with (legal markups for MSA):

- Output Ownership (new clause):
  "4.2 Customer Output. Customer shall retain all right, title and interest in and to Customer Data and the Outputs generated by the Service from Customer Data (\"Customer Outputs\"). For clarity, Redwood's rights are limited to aggregated and anonymized service telemetry and metrics that cannot be reverse-engineered to reconstruct Customer Data or Customer Outputs. Any assignment of derivative rights by Customer is explicitly excluded unless negotiated in writing in a separate statement of work."

- Training / Data Use (Order Form appendix):
  "Order Form Appendix A: No-Training-By-Default. Supplier will not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or otherwise update Supplier models unless Customer executes Appendix B (Model Tuning Addendum) with explicit scope, data retention, and security controls. Appendix B will include auditability requirements and the ability for Customer to withdraw consent for future training activities."

- Feedback License (MSA clause):
  "Feedback License. Customer grants Supplier a worldwide, royalty-free, non-exclusive license to use Feedback provided by Customer, provided that Feedback is de-identified and aggregated such that it cannot be associated back to Customer Data or specific users. Supplier shall not incorporate Customer proprietary outputs into any product offering in a way that reconstitutes Customer Data or reproduces identifiable Customer Outputs."

I will run these through our precedent bank and return a version marked for external review. Laura — if you have precedent tweaks, please add.

Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@stratacorp.com>

Date: Mon, 06 May 2029 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: StrataCorp MSA & Order Form — IP ownership mapping and proposed positions

Alyssa — thanks for the patience. Attached are our proposed redlines and a short extract that maps each of your asks to our language. High level:

- Output: We propose Customer ownership of Outputs, with a carve-out for "aggregated, anonymized telemetry" for Redwood's internal improvement work. No assignment of derivative rights.
- Training: Order Form will include a "No-Training-By-Default" statement; any training requires an opt-in appendix (scope, retention, security, and audit rights).
- Feedback: Limited, de-identified feedback license for internal improvements only; we included explicit examples of prohibited uses to address procurement concerns.

Next steps:
- If this aligns, can StrataCorp Legal confirm whether the prohibition examples are sufficient or if you want different wording?
- If approved, we'll prepare a clean MSA + Order Form and route for DocuSign (link below).

Rachel Kim
